title: FRASE-bot screening identifies a small-molecule ligand that selectively kills CIB1-dependent cancer cells
summary: FRASE-bot used a neural-network nativeness score to triage protein–ligand fragments, then used the retained structural features to seed virtual screening for Calcium and Integrin Binding Protein 1 (CIB1). Of 56 purchased virtual-screen hits, 29 showed dose-dependent CIB1 displacement; compound UNC10245380 (UNC5380) had a TR-FRET displacement IC50 of 8.0 ± 2.5 μM and selectively killed CIB1-depletion-sensitive triple-negative breast cancer cells in the reported assays, with no detected killing in an insensitive line.
ai_technology: FRASE-bot: fragment-in-structural-environment screening with a neural-network nativeness scoring model
organization: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; University of Missouri

evidence.tested: Of 56 purchased virtual-screen hits, 29 showed dose-dependent CIB1 displacement; compound UNC10245380 (UNC5380) had a TR-FRET displacement IC50 of 8.0 ± 2.5 μM and selectively killed CIB1-depletion-sensitive triple-negative breast cancer cells in the reported assays, with no detected killing in an insensitive line.
evidence.unknown: The authors describe UNC10245380 as a starting chemical probe/lead, not a drug. Binding was inferred from peptide displacement in TR-FRET and a docking pose; the pose is not a solved small-molecule complex. Selective cell killing was in vitro at 30 μM, with no animal or clinical evidence. The earlier Research Square manuscript is the same underlying paper/result and is not counted separately.
evidence.ai_role: The neural network triaged fragments by predicted native-ligand pose likelihood; selected fragments informed pharmacophore construction and virtual screening. The resulting purchased compounds were then tested in TR-FRET binding-displacement and cell-death assays. The model did not perform the wet-lab validation.
